stories.headline: World oil market is returning to surplus as Gulf exports recover, IEA says
stories.summary: The IEA reports that global oil markets are moving toward surplus conditions as Gulf producers ramp up exports. This shift suggests near-term relief in commodity prices despite geopolitical tensions.
stories.why_matters: Lower energy costs ease inflation pressures and support consumer spending and corporate margins.

stories.headline: Iran says tanker carrying LNG hit mine, suffered explosion in Hormuz
stories.summary: An Iranian LNG tanker reported hitting a mine and sustaining an explosion in the Strait of Hormuz. This incident escalates regional tensions and could threaten global energy supply routes.
stories.why_matters: Disruption to Hormuz transit risks spiking oil prices and widening geopolitical risk premiums across equities.

stories.headline: Nvidia scandal draws in Commerce Secretary Lutnick, who reportedly agrees to testify about China chip sales
stories.summary: Commerce Secretary Lutnick has agreed to testify about Nvidia's China chip sales amid an ongoing scandal. This development signals potential regulatory scrutiny on semiconductor exports and geopolitical trade policy.
stories.why_matters: Semiconductor export restrictions could reshape tech sector margins and US-China trade dynamics, pressuring large-cap equities.

calendar.note: Fed communications on rates and policy stance could drive Treasury yields and equity volatility given already-elevated 2Y/10Y moves today.
EPU index release may reflect heightened geopolitical and regulatory risks evident in today's Iran/Nvidia headlines and VIX uptick.

concept.title: Risk-Off Rotation amid Geopolitical & Regulatory Uncertainty
concept.one_liner: Equities decline while bond yields rise and volatility spikes as Iran tensions and tech regulation clouds sentiment.
concept.explanation: The S&P 500 fell 1.06% while the VIX rose 1.21 points on Friday morning, driven by geopolitical escalation (Iranian tanker incident), regulatory uncertainty (Nvidia/China chip sales scrutiny), and a steeper yield curve (2Y +17 bps, 10Y +10 bps). EUR/USD weakened as the dollar strengthened, typical of risk-off conditions. Headline risks from Hormuz transit disruptions and semiconductor export policy are elevating policy uncertainty and pulling money into safer rates.
concept.market_link: When equity risk premiums widen and yields climb on policy uncertainty, investors typically rotate from stocks to Treasuries and higher-quality assets—a pattern consistent with today's -1.06% S&P move paired with rising VIX and steeper yields.

narrative: US equities opened down 1.06% on Friday as geopolitical tensions (Iran tanker incident, IAEA concerns), regulatory headwinds (Nvidia China chip testimony), and higher Treasury yields (2Y +17 bps, 10Y +10 bps) triggered a risk-off shift. The VIX climbed to 18.70, the dollar strengthened (EUR/USD -0.0036), and a weakening oil market surplus outlook failed to offset broader uncertainty, signaling cautious sentiment ahead of FOMC communications today.
